error_bridge.desc_specialized_repair_ready: I noticed you've made mistakes on 「{cluster_label}」 {streak_count} times in a row. Let's pause new content. I've prepared a {minutes}-minute specialized repair task. You can schedule it for today or tomorrow.
error_bridge.generic_repair_state_transition: Redraw the complete state/process diagram, marking triggers and transition conditions for each step.
error_bridge.generic_repair_unit_conversion: List unit conversion relationships first, then do 2 similar problems writing out each conversion step.
error_bridge.generic_repair_formula_application: Write the formula and applicable conditions first, then do 2 similar problems verifying only formula selection and substitution.
error_bridge.recurring_cause_confusion_hypothesis: Repeatedly confusing trigger conditions for state transitions suggests you may not yet understand the protocol state machine as an "event-driven design constraint" rather than just forgetting individual state names.
error_bridge.recurring_cause_confusion_intervention: Pause similar problems. Spend 20 minutes rebuilding the state machine from TCP's design goals: clarify each state's purpose, then annotate each transition with trigger packet, active/passive role, and why the switch is necessary.
error_bridge.recurring_cause_transition_hypothesis: Repeated errors in state transitions suggest state names, events, and timing haven't been bound into a complete causal map yet.
error_bridge.recurring_cause_transition_intervention: Redraw the complete state diagram for one protocol flow using a three-column table: "current state + sent/received + next state".
error_bridge.recurring_cause_boundary_hypothesis: Same error cause reappearing suggests adjacent concept boundaries haven't stabilized, not insufficient practice volume.
error_bridge.recurring_cause_boundary_intervention: Create a comparison table separating easily confused concepts by definition, trigger conditions, and typical cues, then do 1 transfer check problem.
error_bridge.recurring_cause_fallback_hypothesis: In the last 30 days, the same cause "{cause}" has recurred on {node_id}. This suggests an incomplete understanding structure rather than a one-time careless mistake.
error_bridge.recurring_cause_fallback_intervention: Pause similar problems. Spend 15-20 minutes returning to the concept's design purpose, judgment criteria, and counterexample boundaries. Finish with 1 similar problem to verify the cause is resolved.
error_bridge.repair_step_review: Review the last {count} errors and identify the single trigger point where you keep getting stuck on this type of problem.
error_bridge.repair_step_final_check: Complete 1 similar check problem, verifying only whether this error cluster has been addressed.
error_bridge.repair_success_criteria: Be able to explain the judgment criteria for 「{cluster_label}」 and complete 1 similar check problem.
error_bridge.repair_objective: Only tackle 「{cluster_label}」 — do not advance to new content.
error_bridge.repair_micro_contract: Pause new content; only fix this error cluster. Don't switch to a second topic until this is clear.
error_bridge.repair_fail_safe_rule: This card is only for the current error cluster. Do not expand to full chapter review.
error_bridge.repair_output_process_trace: Redraw a state/sequence diagram for 「{cluster_label}」 and complete 1 similar check problem.
error_bridge.repair_output_calculation_drill: Complete 2 similar problems verifying only 「{cluster_label}」 and write out the reasoning for each step.
error_bridge.repair_output_comparison_table: Create a comparison table for 「{cluster_label}」 and explain the key differences in your own words.
error_bridge.repair_output_concept_recall: Closed-book recall of the key judgment points for 「{cluster_label}」 and complete 1 minimal check.
error_bridge.repair_ai_prompt_help_1: 1. Focus only on this error cluster, don't expand to the whole chapter.
error_bridge.repair_ai_prompt_help_2: 2. Give the shortest correction path first, then 1 similar check problem.
error_bridge.repair_ai_prompt_help_3: 3. If I get it wrong, keep fixing only this point, don't switch question types.

error_bridge.plan_adjusted_desc_fallback: You've had {count} issues on the same knowledge point recently. I've fine-tuned this week's plan.

insight.night_energy_mismatch_desc: You often schedule high-cognitive-load studying during your low-energy hours, investing time without truly absorbing.
insight.night_energy_mismatch_solution: Move the most demanding tasks to your two most alert hours. Keep evenings for review, organization, and light practice.
insight.perfectionism_avoidance_desc: Thinking you need to do it perfectly before starting makes it harder to begin, pushing important tasks further back.
insight.perfectionism_avoidance_solution: Compress tasks into a 10-minute minimal version that only requires starting, not perfection.
insight.perfectionism_paralysis_desc: You tend to repeatedly measure standards before starting, getting stuck in preparation and never reaching actual execution.
insight.perfectionism_paralysis_solution: Deliver a rough working version first, then schedule a second round of refinement. Replace one-shot perfection with two-stage progress.
insight.idealistic_scheduling_desc: Plans are packed full without buffers for fluctuation, catch-up, or interruptions, making derailment almost certain.
insight.idealistic_scheduling_solution: Keep only 1 core task and 1 fallback task per day, reserving at least 20% buffer time.
insight.planning_optimism_desc: You tend to underestimate task duration and overestimate what you can accomplish in a day.
insight.planning_optimism_solution: Multiply key tasks' estimated time by 1.5 when planning, then decide whether to add more.
insight.focus_decay_desc: You experience noticeable distraction or efficiency drop soon after starting, making learning quality front-heavy.
insight.focus_decay_solution: Break long tasks into 25-40 minute segments. Between segments, stand up, change environment, or do a brief review.
insight.doubt_revision_loop_desc: You tend to doubt yourself immediately after an initial judgment, frequently revisiting and revising, consuming momentum and decision confidence.
insight.doubt_revision_loop_solution: Set a 'first answer commitment' for key problems: complete the first version within a time limit, then do only one round of necessary revision.
insight.cognitive_blindspot_desc: You've formed a stable misconception that's hard to notice in the moment, causing repeated mistakes in similar scenarios.
insight.cognitive_blindspot_solution: After each mistake, add 'What did I assume just now?' and write the blindspot as a refutable statement.
